user.title: UniFi Gateway
user.description: Connect to your UniFi OS gateway (UCG/UDM/UXG) on your local network.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the gateway console.
data_description.tls_mode: UniFi OS ships a self-signed certificate. Pinning records the one it serves now and refuses any other; the next screen shows it so you can compare it with the console.

tls_fingerprint.title: Trust this certificate
tls_fingerprint.description:
The gateway is serving a certificate with this SHA-256 fingerprint:

`{fingerprint}`

Compare it with the one the console shows before continuing. From now on only this certificate is accepted.

This assumes the connection you are looking at right now is not already being intercepted — it is not the same assurance as a certificate signed by a public authority.

tls_fingerprint_changed.title: This is not the certificate on file
tls_fingerprint_changed.description:
This entry pinned:

`{previous}`

The gateway is now serving:

`{fingerprint}`

A reissued certificate looks exactly like an impersonated one from here. Continue only if you replaced the certificate yourself, or can compare this value with the console's own screen. Continuing replaces the pinned certificate.

api_key.title: API key
api_key.description: Create a key in the UniFi OS UI: Settings → Control Plane → Integrations → Create API Key.

password.title: Local account
password.description: Use a local UniFi OS account (not a Ubiquiti SSO/cloud login).

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description: Your saved credentials stopped working. Enter them again.

error.cert_mismatch: The gateway presented a different certificate than the one this entry pinned. Nothing was sent to it — resolve the certificate warning first.
error.insufficient_permissions: This credential cannot read the gateway API. Use a local account or a full-access API key.

abort.wrong_device: The credentials are for a different gateway than the one configured.

data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll the gateway (15–3600 s; default 30).
data_description.enable_controls: Adds write buttons. Requires write-capable auth (a local account, or an API key created with write scope).

confirm.title: The certificate of {host} changed
confirm.description:
This entry accepts only:

`{expected}`

The gateway is serving:

`{got}`

Either the certificate was reissued, or something is impersonating the gateway. Compare the new value with the console's own screen before accepting it — credentials are withheld while the certificate does not match.

Accepting pins the new certificate and reloads the integration.

abort.cannot_connect: The gateway could not be reached, so its certificate could not be re-read. Nothing was changed.
abort.entry_not_found: That configuration entry no longer exists.

tls_insecure.title: {host} is set up without certificate checks

confirm.title: Start checking the certificate of {host}
confirm.description:
This entry was created before certificate pinning existed and accepts any certificate, so nothing proves the host answering is your gateway.

The gateway is serving:

`{fingerprint}`

Compare it with the console's own screen, then accept it to pin it. Pinning assumes this connection is not already being intercepted — it is not the same assurance as a certificate signed by a public authority.

You can also dismiss this and carry on unverified.

abort.cannot_connect: The gateway could not be reached, so its certificate could not be read. Nothing was changed.
abort.entry_not_found: That configuration entry no longer exists.

options.ca: Verify against the system CA store

action_auth_failed.message: The action failed to authenticate. Re-check your credentials.

action_not_permitted.message: This credential is not permitted to perform control actions. Use a write-capable account or API key.

action_cannot_connect.message: Could not reach the gateway to perform the action.
